title: Practice Exam 1
description: 10 free-response coding challenges covering File I/O, static fields, encapsulation & bounds, interfaces & polymorphism, overloading & constructor chaining, composition, exception-handling input loops, file processing, inheritance & super, and instanceof downcasting.

questions.title: Hello File
questions.prompt:
Write a program that creates `hello.txt` holding exactly these three lines:

```
Hello, file!
This is BoilerCS.
Goodbye.
```

Each line ends with a line break (`\n`), including the last. If `hello.txt` already exists, the program replaces its contents completely (do not append). The program prints nothing to the screen (`System.out` and `System.err` must remain completely silent). `Main.java` holds an empty `main`; the whole program is yours to write.

Use try-with-resources so the file handle is closed (and flushed) cleanly.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: File hello.txt created with exact 3 lines and terminal newline.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Overwrite Verification)
tests.description: If hello.txt already contained 1,000 lines of old text, the new file is truncated to exactly 3 lines with zero remnant bytes.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Strict Linebreak Encoding)
tests.description: All lines end with \n and contain no \r\n artifacts or trailing space padding on "Goodbye.".

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Silence Check)
tests.description: Output streams emit 0 bytes; printing status or error messages fails this test.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Flush Guarantee)
tests.description: File handles closed properly (try-with-resources); unclosed streams that delay flushing fail.

graderCases.name: Sample run (exact three lines + terminal newline)
Overwrite truncates old content
No carriage returns, no trailing padding

questions.title: Spacecraft
questions.prompt:
Implement the class `Spacecraft` in `Spacecraft.java`; the starter file holds method signatures only. All fields must be private.

* A spacecraft knows its callsign (a `String`) and its thrust in kilonewtons (a `double`).
* `Spacecraft(String callsign, double thrust)` stores both and increments the count of spacecraft created.
* `getCallsign()` and `getThrust()` return the fields; `setThrust(double thrust)` changes the thrust.
* `static int getCount()` returns how many `Spacecraft` objects have been created since the program started.
* Calling getters, setters, or passing invalid values does **not** alter `getCount()`.
* `Main.java` is a test driver; do not edit it.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 2 instances created, getters return fields, setter mutates thrust, getCount() returns 2.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Null Callsign Handling)
tests.description: new Spacecraft(null, 10.0) increments getCount() and stores null cleanly without NullPointerException.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Negative Thrust)
tests.description: Setting thrust to -5.0 or 0.0 updates the thrust without modifying getCount().

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Field Encapsulation & Shadowing)
tests.description: Fields are private and non-static, while count is private static.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Static Access Decoupling)
tests.description: Calling Spacecraft.getCount() before any constructor calls returns 0.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Multiple Mutation Stability)
tests.description: Repeated calls to setThrust() on the same instance never affect the static count.

graderCases.name: Sample run (getters, setter, count)
Null callsign increments count cleanly
Negative/zero thrust does not change count
Fields private non-static, count private static
Multiple mutations keep count stable

questions.title: Thermostat
questions.prompt:
Write the class `Thermostat` in `Thermostat.java`; the file holds signatures only. All fields must be private.

* A thermostat's temperature is an integer level from 50 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit inclusive.
* `setLevel(int level)` stores the value only if it is in range `[50, 90]`; an out-of-range value changes nothing (retains previous valid level).
* The constructor `Thermostat(int level)` routes its argument through `setLevel`. Because fields initialize to default values (0 for int), an invalid constructor argument leaves the level at `50` (the lower bound default fallback).
* `getLevel()` returns the level.
* `up()` raises the level by 1 unless it is already 90 (clamped).
* `down()` lowers the level by 1 unless it is already 50 (clamped).
* `Main.java` is a test driver; do not edit it.

*Hint:* initialize the field to `50` so that an invalid constructor argument leaves the level at `50`.

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Up raises level, out-of-range 105 rejected, bad starting value 45 defaults to 50.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Boundary Clamping at 90)
tests.description: At level 90, calling up() ten times keeps level at exactly 90.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Boundary Clamping at 50)
tests.description: At level 50, calling down() ten times keeps level at exactly 50.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Off-by-One Constructor Rejection)
tests.description: new Thermostat(49) and new Thermostat(91) default to 50.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Off-by-One Setter Rejection)
tests.description: At level 70, calling setLevel(49) and setLevel(91) preserves 70.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Exact In-Range Edges)
tests.description: new Thermostat(50) gives 50; new Thermostat(90) gives 90. setLevel(50) and setLevel(90) update successfully.

graderCases.name: Sample run (up, reject 105, default 45->50)
Clamp at 90
Clamp at 50
Off-by-one constructor rejection
graderCases.body:
eq(new Thermostat(49).getLevel(), 50);
eq(new Thermostat(91).getLevel(), 50);

graderCases.name: Off-by-one setter rejection
Exact in-range edges

questions.title: Renewable Grid
questions.prompt:
Files given (read-only): `PowerSource.java` (an interface with `String sourceName()` and `double dailyOutputKWh()`), `WindTurbine.java` and `SolarArray.java` (implement `PowerSource`), and `Main.java` (driver). They are provided as extra tabs so your code compiles — do not edit them.

Write `RenewableGrid.java`, which contains two static methods working for **any** `PowerSource`:
* `static double totalOutput(PowerSource[] sources)` returns the sum of every `dailyOutputKWh()`.
* `static String primarySource(PowerSource[] sources)` returns the `sourceName()` of the element with the largest `dailyOutputKWh()`.
  * **Tie-Breaking Trap:** If multiple sources share the highest output, the **first one encountered** in array order wins.
  * **Drawdown Trap:** A `dailyOutputKWh()` may be negative (battery storage recharging drawdown).
  * **Empty Array Trap:** An empty array (`length == 0`) returns `0.0` for total and `""` for primary.
  * **Null Element Trap:** If an element in `sources` is `null`, skip it without throwing `NullPointerException`.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Sparse Array with Nulls)

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (All Negative Outputs)
tests.description: Sources with outputs {-150.0, -40.0, -90.0}: primary must be -40.0, not 0.0 or -150.0.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Exact Floating Point Tie)
tests.description: Two sources with identical output of 300.0 returns the first source's name.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Array of Only Nulls)
tests.description: {null, null} returns 0.0 and "".

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Empty Array)

questions.title: Package Shipment Overloading
questions.prompt:
Implement `Shipment.java` with private fields: `String destination`, `double weightLbs`, and `boolean express`.

Implement constructor and method overloading:
* `Shipment(String destination, double weightLbs, boolean express)`: stores all three fields.
* `Shipment(String destination, double weightLbs)`: overloads constructor, defaulting `express` to `false` (chain using `this(...)`).
* `Shipment(String destination)`: overloads constructor, defaulting `weightLbs` to `1.0` and `express` to `false` (chain using `this(...)`).
* `getDestination()`, `getWeightLbs()`, and `isExpress()` return the fields.
* `calculateCost()` computes shipping cost as `$5.00 + (weightLbs * 1.50)`. If `express` is true, add a flat `$10.00` surcharge.
* `calculateCost(double discountDollar)`: overloads `calculateCost()` by subtracting `discountDollar`.
  * **Negative Cost Floor:** If calculated cost drops below `0.0`, clamp to `0.0`.
  * **Negative Discount Trap:** If `discountDollar < 0.0`, treat `discountDollar` as `0.0` (do not increase price).

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 3-arg, 1-arg defaults, base cost, and discount overload with 0.0 floor.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Negative Discount Trap)
tests.description: Calling calculateCost(-15.0) does not add $15 to the cost; returns base cost.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Zero Weight Package)
tests.description: Package with 0.0 lbs non-express costs base fee $5.00.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Constructor Delegation Enforcement)
tests.description: Constructors chain via this(...).

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Exact Cost Discount)
tests.description: Discount equal to cost produces exactly 0.0.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Double Precision Handling)
tests.description: Weight of 3.33 lbs calculated without truncated integer arithmetic.

graderCases.name: Sample run (overloads + floor)
Negative discount treated as 0
graderCases.body:
Shipment s = new Shipment("X", 4.0, true);
eqD(s.calculateCost(-15.0), 21.0);

graderCases.name: Zero weight non-express base fee
graderCases.body:
Shipment s = new Shipment("X", 0.0);
eqD(s.calculateCost(), 5.0);

graderCases.name: Exact cost discount gives 0
graderCases.body:
Shipment s = new Shipment("X", 0.0);
eqD(s.calculateCost(5.0), 0.0);

graderCases.name: Double precision weight
graderCases.body:
Shipment s = new Shipment("X", 3.33);
eqD(s.calculateCost(), 5.0 + 3.33 * 1.5);

questions.title: Subscription Account
questions.prompt:
`User.java` is given and complete: `User(String username, boolean student)` with `getUsername()`, `isStudent()`, and `setStudent(boolean student)`. It is provided as an extra tab — do not edit it.

Implement `Subscription.java`; all fields must be private:
* `Subscription(User user, int months, double monthlyRate)` stores all three fields.
* `getUser()` and `getMonths()` return the fields; `setMonths(int months)` changes the months.
* `totalCost()` is `months * monthlyRate`. A student user pays 20% less (`0.80 * total`).
  * **Dynamic Delegation Trap:** `totalCost()` **must query** `user.isStudent()` each time it is called.
* `toString()` returns exactly: `Subscription[<username>, <months> months, $<totalCost formatted to 2 decimals>]`. Use the word `months` even if months is 1.

questions.title: Robust Port Number
questions.prompt:
Write a program in `Main.java`:

Ask `Enter port: ` until the user enters a whole number from `1024` to `65535` inclusive.
* For any input that cannot be parsed as an integer (e.g., text, floating-point numbers, empty line), print `Not a number.`.
* For any integer outside `1024` to `65535`, print `Out of range.`.
* When an acceptable port is entered, print `Port: ` followed by the port, and then on the next line print `Attempts: ` followed by the total number of attempts.
* Every prompt counts as one attempt, including rejected attempts and the final accepted attempt.
* **Crash-Proof Trap:** The program must handle leading/trailing spaces, massive numbers exceeding `Integer.MAX_VALUE` (e.g., `999999999999`), and blank inputs without crashing.

*Enter one input per line in the stdin box (the bracketed values in the sample).*
questions.sampleRun:
Enter port: http
Not a number.
Enter port: 80
Out of range.
Enter port: 8080
Port: 8080
Attempts: 3
questions.expectedOutput:
Enter port: Not a number.
Enter port: Out of range.
Enter port: Port: 8080
Attempts: 3

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: Non-number, out of range, valid entry, 3 attempts. Provide stdin: http / 80 / 8080.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Integer Overflow Input)
tests.description: Entering 999999999999 prints Not a number. without crashing.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Whitespace Padding)
tests.description: Input "  8080  " parses cleanly as 8080.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Exact Inclusive Bounds)
tests.description: 1024 and 65535 accepted on attempt 1.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Exact Off-by-One Rejections)
tests.description: 1023 and 65536 print Out of range..

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Negative Numbers)
tests.description: -8080 prints Out of range. (valid integer, out of bounds).

tests.name: Test 7 [Hidden] (Float/Double Trap)
tests.description: 8080.0 prints Not a number..

questions.title: Server Response Times
questions.prompt:
`latencies.txt` holds one server ping latency in milliseconds per line: a positive whole number. Read the file and write `metrics.txt` holding exactly these four lines:

```
Pings: <count>
Average: <average with exactly 2 decimal places>
Slowest: <maximum value>
Exceeds threshold: <number of pings strictly greater than 100>
```

If `latencies.txt` cannot be opened or does not exist, print exactly one line to the screen: `Cannot open latencies.txt.`, write no report file, and terminate without crashing. `Main.java` holds an empty `main`; write your solution there.

*The grader creates `latencies.txt` before running your code.*

tests.name: Test 1 [Visible] (Sample Run)
tests.description: 5 lines processed, 2-decimal average, max latency, count strictly > 100.

tests.name: Test 2 [Hidden] (Missing File Clean Failure)
tests.description: Missing file prints Cannot open latencies.txt. to console, creates NO metrics.txt, exits cleanly.

tests.name: Test 3 [Hidden] (Strict Greater-Than Threshold)
tests.description: Ping of exactly 100 is not counted in Exceeds threshold.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Single-Line File)
tests.description: File with only 42 computes Pings: 1, Average: 42.00, Slowest: 42, Exceeds: 0.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Rounding Boundary)
tests.description: Average formatted with %.2f rounds per standard double formatting.

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Trailing Blank Lines)
tests.description: File with empty trailing lines does not crash or inflate ping count.

questions.title: Senior Project Leader
questions.prompt:
`Student.java` is given and complete: `Student(String name, double gpa)` with `getName()`, `getGpa()`, `double stipend(int credits)` (calculated as `credits * 50.0`), and `toString()` returning `<name> (<gpa> GPA)`. It has no zero-argument constructor. It is provided as an extra tab — do not edit it.

Write `ProjectLeader.java`: a project leader **is a** `Student` with a leadership grant.
* `ProjectLeader(String name, double gpa, double leadershipGrant)`.
* `getLeadershipGrant()` returns the grant.
* `stipend(int credits)`: returns the student stipend for those credits plus the leadership grant added once.
  * **Super Delegation Constraint:** The override **must** call `super.stipend(credits)`.
* `toString()` returns the student description followed by ` (leader)`.
  * **Super Delegation Constraint:** The override **must** build on `super.toString()`.
* All new fields must be private.

questions.title: Animal Shelter Registry
questions.prompt:
`Animal.java`, `Dog.java`, and `Cat.java` are given and read-only (provided as extra tabs):
* `Animal(String name)` with `getName()`.
* `Dog extends Animal`: has method `String getBreed()`.
* `Cat extends Animal`: has method `boolean isIndoor()`.
* The test cases also use other subclasses of `Animal` you have never seen (e.g., `Bird extends Animal`).

Write `ShelterRegistry.java` containing two static methods:
* `static String identify(Animal a)`:
  * If `a` is a `Dog`, returns `Dog: ` followed by its breed (e.g. `Dog: Golden`).
  * If `a` is a `Cat`, returns `Cat (indoor)` if `isIndoor()` is true, or `Cat (outdoor)` if false.
  * For any other `Animal`, returns `Animal: ` followed by its name (e.g. `Animal: Pip`).
* `static int countDogs(Animal[] animals)`: returns how many elements in the array are instances of `Dog`.
* **Null Safety Trap:** If `animals` contains `null` elements, skip them. If `a` passed to `identify` is `null`, return `"None"`.

tests.description: Identifies Dog, indoor Cat, base Animal; counts 1 dog in array.

tests.name: Test 4 [Hidden] (Subclass of Dog)
tests.description: GuideDog extends Dog is counted as a Dog and returns Dog: <breed>.

tests.name: Test 5 [Hidden] (Cat Outdoor Condition)
tests.description: Cat with isIndoor() == false returns Cat (outdoor).

tests.name: Test 6 [Hidden] (Empty Array)
tests.description: new Animal[0] returns 0.
